tractābĭlĭtas , ātis, f. tractabilis,
I.fitness for being handled or wrought, manageableness, tractability (very rare): “populus, salix, tilia in sculpturis commodam praestant tractabilitatem,” Vitr. 2, 9, 12 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
